1.text_clean:
1. The radius of a circle is measured to be $(10.0 \pm 0.5)$ cm. What is the area of the circle?
A. $(314.2 \pm 0.3)\ \text{cm}^2$
B. $(314 \pm 1)\ \text{cm}^2$
C. $(314 \pm 15)\ \text{cm}^2$
D. $(314 \pm 31)\ \text{cm}^2$

2.text_clean:
2. Two different experiments, P and Q, generate two sets of data to confirm the proportionality of variables $x$ and $y$. The graphs for the data from P and Q are shown. The maximum and minimum gradient lines are shown for both sets of data.
[Graphs: two plots P and Q of y (0 to 3.0) against x (0 to 1.0), each with maximum and minimum gradient lines. In P the lines cross near (0.15, 0.9) and do not pass near the origin; in Q the lines cross near (0.15, 0.3), close to the origin, and diverge more widely (ending near y = 2.9 and y = 1.7 at x = 1.0).]
What is true about the systematic error and the uncertainty of the gradient when P is compared to Q?
Systematic error | Uncertainty of the gradient
A. larger for set P | larger for set P
B. larger for set Q | larger for set P
C. larger for set P | larger for set Q
D. larger for set Q | larger for set Q

3.text_clean:
3. An object is sliding from rest down a frictionless inclined plane. The object slides 1.0 m during the first second.
[Diagram: block on an inclined plane; dashed block 1.0 m further down the slope]
What distance will the object slide during the next second?
A. 1.0 m
B. 2.0 m
C. 3.0 m
D. 4.9 m

4.text_clean:
4. A ball is thrown upwards at time $t = 0$. The graph shows the variation with time of the height of the ball. The ball returns to the initial height at time $T$.
[Graph: parabolic height–time curve from 0 at t = 0 back to 0 at time T; height h marked at time t, after the maximum]
What is the height $h$ at time $t$?
A. $\frac{1}{2}gt^2$
B. $\frac{1}{2}gT^2$
C. $\frac{1}{2}gT(T-t)$
D. $\frac{1}{2}gt(T-t)$

5.text_clean:
5. A solid metal ball is dropped from a tower. The variation with time of the velocity of the ball is plotted.
[Graph: velocity against time, rising from 0 and curving towards a terminal value]
A hollow metal ball with the same size and shape is dropped from the same tower. What graph will represent the variation with time of the velocity for the hollow metal ball?
[Graph: four velocity–time curves A, B, C, D compared with the dashed curve for the solid metal ball; A rises well above it, B slightly above, C levels off slightly below, D much lower with smaller initial gradient]

6.text_clean:
6. A rocket has just been launched vertically from Earth. The image shows the free-body diagram of the rocket. $F_1$ represents a larger force than $F_2$.
[Diagram: dot with upward arrow $F_1$ and shorter downward arrow $F_2$]
Which force pairs with $F_1$ and which force pairs with $F_2$, according to Newton's third law?
Force pair with $F_1$ | Force pair with $F_2$
A. force of rocket on exhaust gases | force of exhaust gases on rocket
B. force of rocket on exhaust gases | gravitational force of rocket on Earth
C. gravitational force of Earth on rocket | force of exhaust gases on rocket
D. gravitational force of Earth on rocket | gravitational force of rocket on Earth

7.text_clean:
7. A book of mass $m$ lies on top of a table of mass $M$ that rolls freely along the ground. The coefficient of friction between the book and the table is $\mu$. A person is pushing the rolling table.
What is the maximum acceleration of the table so that the book does not slide backwards relative to the table?
[Diagram: person pushing a wheeled table of mass M with a book of mass m on top]
A. $\frac{g}{\mu}$
B. $\mu g$
C. $\frac{mg}{M\mu}$
D. $\frac{m}{M}\mu g$

8.text_clean:
8. Two blocks of different masses are released from identical springs of elastic constant $k = 100\ \text{N m}^{-1}$, initially compressed a distance $\Delta x = 0.1$ m. Block X has a mass of 1 kg and block Y has a mass of 0.25 kg.
What are the velocities of the blocks when they leave the springs?
Velocity of block X | Velocity of block Y
A. $1.0\ \text{m s}^{-1}$ | $1.0\ \text{m s}^{-1}$
B. $2.0\ \text{m s}^{-1}$ | $1.0\ \text{m s}^{-1}$
C. $1.0\ \text{m s}^{-1}$ | $2.0\ \text{m s}^{-1}$
D. $2.0\ \text{m s}^{-1}$ | $2.0\ \text{m s}^{-1}$

9.text_clean:
9. What is true for an ideal gas?
A. $nRT = Nk_BT$
B. $nRT = k_BT$
C. $RT = Nk_BT$
D. $RT = k_BT$

10.text_clean:
10. Which assumption is part of the molecular kinetic model of ideal gases?
A. The work done on a system equals the change in kinetic energy of the system.
B. The volume of a gas results from adding the volume of the individual molecules.
C. A gas is made up of tiny identical particles in constant random motion.
D. All particles in a gas have kinetic and potential energy.

11.text_clean:
11. Water at room temperature is placed in a freezer. The specific heat capacity of water is twice the specific heat capacity of ice. Assume that thermal energy is transferred from the water at a constant rate.
Which graph shows the variation with time of the temperature of the water?
[Graphs: four temperature T against time t graphs, each with a falling section, a horizontal plateau and a final falling section. A: first and last slopes equal and gentle; B: gentle first slope, steeper last slope; C: steep first slope, steep last slope; D: steep first slope, gentle last slope]

12.text_clean:
12. A particle undergoes simple harmonic motion. Which quantities of the motion can be simultaneously zero?
A. Displacement and velocity
B. Displacement and acceleration
C. Velocity and acceleration
D. Displacement, velocity and acceleration

13.text_clean:
13. A wave travels along a string. Graph M shows the variation with time of the displacement of a point X on the string. Graph N shows the variation with distance of the displacement of the string. PQ and RS are marked on the graphs.
[Graph M: displacement against time, sinusoidal; P and Q mark two successive crests (one period apart)]
[Graph N: displacement against distance, sinusoidal; R and S mark two points one wavelength apart]
What is the speed of the wave?
A. $\frac{PQ}{RS}$
B. $PQ \times RS$
C. $\frac{RS}{PQ}$
D. $\frac{1}{PQ \times RS}$

14.text_clean:
14. The refractive index of glass is $\frac{3}{2}$ and the refractive index of water is $\frac{4}{3}$. What is the critical angle for light travelling from glass to water?
A. $\sin^{-1}\left(\frac{1}{2}\right)$
B. $\sin^{-1}\left(\frac{2}{3}\right)$
C. $\sin^{-1}\left(\frac{3}{4}\right)$
D. $\sin^{-1}\left(\frac{8}{9}\right)$

15.text_clean:
15. Unpolarized light with an intensity of $320\ \text{W m}^{-2}$ goes through a polarizer and an analyser, originally aligned parallel.
[Diagram: light passing through a polarizer and an analyser with parallel vertical transmission axes]
The analyser is rotated through an angle $\theta = 30°$. $\cos 30° = \frac{\sqrt{3}}{2}$.
[Diagram: same arrangement with the analyser axis rotated by θ from the vertical]
What is the intensity of the light emerging from the analyser?
A. $120\ \text{W m}^{-2}$
B. $80\sqrt{3}\ \text{W m}^{-2}$
C. $240\ \text{W m}^{-2}$
D. $160\sqrt{3}\ \text{W m}^{-2}$

16.text_clean:
16. Four particles, two of charge $+Q$ and two of charge $-Q$, are positioned on the $x$-axis as shown. A particle P with a positive charge is placed on the $y$-axis. What is the direction of the net electrostatic force on this particle?
[Diagram: two −Q charges on the negative x-axis and two +Q charges symmetrically on the positive x-axis; +P on the y-axis with arrows A (up), B (right), C (down), D (left)]

17.text_clean:
17. A battery of negligible internal resistance is connected to a lamp. A second identical lamp is added in series. What is the change in potential difference across the first lamp and what is the change in the output power of the battery?
Change in potential difference | Output power of battery
A. decreases | decreases
B. decreases | increases
C. no change | decreases
D. no change | increases

18.text_clean:
18. A circuit consists of a cell of emf $E = 3.0$ V and four resistors connected as shown. Resistors $R_1$ and $R_4$ are $1.0\ \Omega$ and resistors $R_2$ and $R_3$ are $2.0\ \Omega$.
What is the voltmeter reading?
[Circuit: bridge arrangement across the cell; left branch $R_1 = 1.0\ \Omega$ (top) and $R_3 = 2.0\ \Omega$ (bottom), right branch $R_2 = 2.0\ \Omega$ (top) and $R_4 = 1.0\ \Omega$ (bottom); voltmeter V connected between the midpoints of the two branches]
A. 0.50 V
B. 1.0 V
C. 1.5 V
D. 2.0 V

19.text_clean:
19. The coil of a direct current electric motor is turning with a period $T$. At $t = 0$ the coil is in the position shown in the diagram. Assume the magnetic field is uniform across the coil.
[Diagram: rectangular coil with split-ring commutator between S and N magnet poles; section XY of the coil marked; arrow shows the direction of rotation]
Which graph shows the variation with time of the force exerted on section XY of the coil during one complete turn?
[Graphs of force against time over one period T: A: constant positive, switching to constant negative for the middle half, then positive again; B: constant positive throughout; C: rectified (always positive) sinusoid-like curve; D: cosine-like curve]

20.text_clean:
20. A satellite is orbiting Earth in a circular path at constant speed. Three statements about the resultant force on the satellite are:
I. It is equal to the gravitational force of attraction on the satellite.
II. It is equal to the mass of the satellite multiplied by its acceleration.
III. It is equal to the centripetal force on the satellite.
Which combination of statements is correct?
A. I and II only
B. I and III only
C. II and III only
D. I, II and III

21.text_clean:
21. An astronaut is orbiting Earth in a spaceship. Why does the astronaut experience weightlessness?
A. The astronaut is outside the gravitational field of Earth.
B. The acceleration of the astronaut is the same as the acceleration of the spaceship.
C. The spaceship is travelling at a high speed tangentially to the orbit.
D. The gravitational field is zero at that point.

22.text_clean:
22. White light is emitted from a hot filament. The light passes through hydrogen gas at low pressure and then through a diffraction grating onto a screen. A pattern of lines against a background appears on the screen.
[Diagram: screen showing four lines against a background]
What is the appearance of the lines and background on the screen?
Lines | Background
A. dark | black
B. white | coloured
C. white | black
D. dark | coloured

23.text_clean:
23. Three statements about electrons are:
I. Electrons interact through virtual photons.
II. Electrons interact through gluons.
III. Electrons interact through particles W and Z.
Which statements identify the particles mediating the forces experienced by electrons?
A. I and II only
B. I and III only
C. II and III only
D. I, II and III

24.text_clean:
24. A neutron is absorbed by a nucleus of uranium-235 ($^{235}_{92}\text{U}$). One possible outcome is the production of two nuclides, barium-144 ($^{144}_{56}\text{Ba}$) and krypton-89 ($^{89}_{36}\text{Kr}$).
How many neutrons are released in this reaction?
A. 0
B. 1
C. 2
D. 3

25.text_clean:
25. A radioactive nuclide X decays into a nuclide Y. The graph shows the variation with time of the activity $A$ of X. X and Y have the same nucleon number.
[Graph: activity A against time (0 to 6t), exponential decay; activity falls to half its initial value at 2t]
What is true about nuclide X?
A. alpha ($\alpha$) emitter with a half-life of $t$
B. alpha ($\alpha$) emitter with a half-life of $2t$
C. beta-minus ($\beta^-$) emitter with a half-life of $t$
D. beta-minus ($\beta^-$) emitter with a half-life of $2t$

26.text_clean:
26. Photovoltaic cells and solar heating panels are used to transfer the electromagnetic energy of the Sun's rays into other forms of energy. What is the form of energy into which solar energy is transferred in photovoltaic cells and solar heating panels?
Photovoltaic cells | Solar heating panels
A. electrical energy | thermal energy
B. thermal energy | thermal energy
C. electrical energy | electrical energy
D. thermal energy | electrical energy

27.text_clean:
27. Three statements about fossil fuels are:
I. There is a finite amount of fossil fuels on Earth.
II. The transfer of energy from fossil fuels increases the concentration of $\text{CO}_2$ in the atmosphere.
III. The geographic distribution of fossil fuels is uneven and has led to economic inequalities.
Which statements justify the development of alternative energy sources?
A. I and II only
B. I and III only
C. II and III only
D. I, II and III

28.text_clean:
28. The age of the Earth is about $4.5 \times 10^9$ years.
What area of physics provides experimental evidence for this conclusion?
A. Newtonian mechanics
B. Optics
C. Radioactivity
D. Electromagnetism

29.text_clean:
29. A simple pendulum has a time period $T$ on the Earth. The pendulum is taken to the Moon where the gravitational field strength is $\frac{1}{6}$ that of the Earth.
What is the time period of the pendulum on the Moon?
A. $T\sqrt{6}$
B. $T$
C. $\frac{\sqrt{6}}{6}T$
D. $\frac{T}{6}$

30.text_clean:
30. In two different experiments, white light is passed through a single slit and then is either refracted through a prism or diffracted with a diffraction grating. The prism produces a band of colours from M to N. The diffraction grating produces a first order spectrum P to Q.
[Diagram: left, light through a slit and prism, emerging rays M (less deviated) and N (more deviated); right, light through a slit and diffraction grating, first-order rays P (more deviated) and Q]
What are the colours observed at M and P?
M | P
A. red | red
B. red | violet
C. violet | red
D. violet | violet

31.text_clean:
31. A train is sounding its whistle when approaching a train station. Three statements about the sound received by a stationary observer at the station are:
I. The frequency received is higher than the frequency emitted by the train.
II. The wavelength received is longer than the wavelength emitted by the train.
III. The speed of the sound received is not affected by the motion of the train.
Which combination of statements is correct?
A. I and II only
B. I and III only
C. II and III only
D. I, II and III

32.text_clean:
32. Two positive and two negative charges are located at the corners of a square as shown. Point X is the centre of the square. What is the value of the electric field $E$ and the electric potential $V$ at X due to the four charges?
[Diagram: square with +Q top-left, −Q top-right, −Q bottom-left, +Q bottom-right; X at the centre]
Electric field $E$ at X | Electric potential $V$ at X
A. $E = 0$ | $V = 0$
B. $E \neq 0$ | $V = 0$
C. $E = 0$ | $V \neq 0$
D. $E \neq 0$ | $V \neq 0$

33.text_clean:

[Graph: V against r, decreasing curve approaching zero; distance s marked]
What is the electric field strength at distance s?
A. The area under the graph between s and infinity
B. The area under the graph between 0 and s
C. The gradient of the tangent at s
D. The negative of the gradient of the tangent at s

34.text_clean:
34. Which two features are necessary for the operation of a transformer?
Feature one | Feature two
A. electrical connection between primary and secondary coils | input of alternating current
B. magnetic interaction between primary and secondary coils | input of alternating current
C. electrical connection between primary and secondary coils | input of direct current
D. magnetic interaction between primary and secondary coils | input of direct current

[Diagram: horizontal rectangular bar with P top-left, Q top-right, R bottom-right, S bottom-left, moving down with velocity v in a field B into the page]
Which side of the bar will have the greatest density of electrons?
A. PQ
B. QR
C. RS
D. SP

36.text_clean:
36. A circuit consists of three identical capacitors of capacitance $C$ and a battery of voltage $V$. Two capacitors are connected in parallel with a third in series. The capacitors are fully charged.
[Circuit: battery V in series with capacitor Z and the parallel pair of capacitors X and Y]
What is the charge stored in capacitors X and Z?
Charge stored in capacitor Z | Charge stored in capacitor X
A. $\frac{CV}{3}$ | $\frac{CV}{3}$
B. $\frac{CV}{3}$ | $\frac{2CV}{3}$
C. $\frac{2CV}{3}$ | $\frac{CV}{3}$

I. An electron beam is used to investigate the structure of crystals.
II. An electron beam produces a pattern of fringes when sent through two narrow parallel slits.
III. Electromagnetic radiation ejects electrons from the surface of a metal.
Which statements are explained using the wave-like properties of electrons?
A. I and II only
B. I and III only
C. II and III only
D. I, II and III

A. $\frac{1}{4}$
B. $\frac{1}{2}$
C. 1
D. 4
